news.headline: FOMC Decision Day — US 10Y Yield Touches 5%, Markets Sell Off
news.what_happened: Fed concludes its Sept 15-16 meeting today. US 10-year Treasury yield hit 4.996%, the highest since 2007, triggering a selloff: S&P 500 -0.45%, Nasdaq -0.78%, Dow -0.63%. Traders fear a hawkish hold or rate-hike signal from Powell.
news.why_it_matters: A hawkish Fed strengthens USD, pushes US yields higher, and triggers FII outflows from EMs including India. Rate-sensitive sectors (banks, NBFCs, real estate) face headwinds. FOMC outcome due after Indian market close sets tomorrow's tone.

news.headline: WTI Crude Eases 0.92% to $104.86 — Partial Relief for Paint and Tyre Sectors
news.what_happened: Crude oil fell from yesterday's elevated $105.83 to $104.86 (-0.92%) as the initial shock of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline closure (Houthi drone attacks) partially subsides. Crude remains structurally elevated vs pre-attack levels near $95.
news.why_it_matters: Crude derivatives account for 40-50% of raw material costs for paint companies and 60-70% for tyre makers. Even a sub-1% crude decline provides meaningful margin tailwind. Paints and tyres are the primary beneficiaries today.

news.headline: FII Net Sellers ₹2,978 Cr on Sep 15; DII Supported ₹2,686 Cr
news.what_happened: Foreign institutional investors sold a net ₹2,977.90 Cr in the cash segment Tuesday ahead of FOMC. DIIs absorbed ₹2,686 Cr. Nifty 50 closed at approximately 23,118, down ~1.2% from previous close of 23,398.
news.why_it_matters: Large FII selling ahead of FOMC reflects global risk-off positioning. Stocks with highest FII ownership (HDFCBANK, INFY, TCS, RELIANCE) bear the brunt. DII buying provides a floor but does not reverse the trend alone.

news.headline: China August Data Disappoints — Retail Sales +0.4% vs +0.8% Expected
news.what_happened: China's August retail sales rose just 0.4% YoY vs consensus +0.8%. Fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% for Jan-Aug. Jobless rate ticked up. Only industrial output outperformed. No new stimulus announced.
news.why_it_matters: China is the world's largest consumer of steel, aluminium, and industrial metals. Weak demand signals lower commodity prices globally. Indian metal companies face a bearish backdrop with no stimulus to offset the miss.

news.headline: RBI Endorses UPI MDR on Large Transactions; Tata Sons Listing Made Mandatory
news.what_happened: RBI backed MDR on UPI transactions above ₹2,000 (user-end remains free). Separately, RBI rejected Tata Sons' CIC exemption application, making a public listing mandatory amid leadership turbulence at the group.
news.why_it_matters: UPI MDR is a structural positive for payment ecosystem sustainability. Tata Sons listing mandatory — Tata group stocks may see event-driven volatility. No rate policy signal from RBI.
